about.metaDescription: Marea Baja is a fictional nikkei ceviche restaurant in Barrio Escalante: cooking from Peru meeting Japan, with fish from Costa Rica’s Pacific coast.
about.title: About
about.lead: A nikkei bar designed like a printed menu: few dishes, cut well, with the fish that came in today.
about.originTitle: Peru and Japan on the same board
about.originBody: Nikkei cooking was born where Peruvian and Japanese cooking met: leche de tigre, ají and the cut made to order. That’s the bar’s craft: ceviches, tiraditos, raw dishes, maki rolls and bowls, plus a few dishes from the grill for anyone who’d rather have something hot.
about.seaTitle: What the sea brought in today
about.seaBody: The menu depends on the catch. Every morning we publish the board with the fish that arrived and its port: corvina from Puntarenas, red snapper from the Gulf of Nicoya, tuna from Quepos. When something doesn’t arrive, the dish shows as “Sold out today”.
about.craftBody: We cut when you order and dress at the end, so the dish arrives fresh even when it travels. The bowls are designed for delivery.
about.demoBody: Marea Baja doesn’t exist: it’s a portfolio project. Orders and payments are simulated and no dish is actually prepared.
